blocks.text: 1. Deduplication
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446840770-603293937.png
Deduplication covers how repeated or near identical documents get identified and handled, shifting focus from describing documents to comparing them against each other.
It removes redundant copies before they waste space in the document collection.
2. Why Duplicates Accumulate

The same underlying content often gets ingested more than once, from different sources or repeated runs, whether through web crawling, database ingestion, or API ingestion, as covered in Document Ingestion.
Mirrored pages, re-synced records, and reprocessed files all produce duplicates.

blocks.text: 3. Exact Versus Near Dupes
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446840771-896690152.png
An exact duplicate matches byte for byte; a near duplicate differs only slightly.
These are two different problems, each needing its own detection approach.
4. Hashing For Exact Matches
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446840772-696786619.png
Hashing the full, normalized text of a document produces a compact fingerprint.
Two documents with the same hash are exact duplicates.

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: Hashing after normalization, as covered in Text Normalization, matters here: two documents that differ only in casing or whitespace would produce different hashes on raw text, but the same hash once normalized first.

blocks.text: 5. Similarity For Near Dupes
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446840772-310972464.png
Near duplicates need a similarity measure rather than an exact hash comparison.
Just as What Is RAG covers retrieval using embeddings, embedding similarity can also detect near duplicate documents.
6. Duplicates Across Sources
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446840772-919721852.png
The same article can be crawled from one site and also pulled through an API from another.
Deduplication has to work across sources, not just within a single one.

blocks.title: warn
blocks.content: Deduplicating only within a single ingestion run misses duplicates introduced across separate runs or separate sources entirely, so a persistent fingerprint store needs to span the whole collection.

blocks.text: 7. Why Dupes Hurt Retrieval
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446840773-110013452.png
Duplicate chunks crowd out diverse, useful results in a retrieval system's top matches.
This wastes both storage and the retrieved context a model actually sees.

blocks.text: 8. Deduping Before Or After Chunking
Deduplicating whole documents first is cheaper than deduplicating every individual chunk.
This catches duplicates early, before chunking, covered as a later module, even begins.
9. Recognizing When Deduplication Deserves Careful Attention

blocks.alt: Recognizing When Deduplication Deserves Careful Attention
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446840773-99871627.png
Pipelines pulling from multiple overlapping sources need thorough deduplication.
A single, tightly controlled source, by contrast, needs only light deduplication.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Hashing raw, unnormalized text and missing duplicates that differ only in casing or whitespace.
Only checking for exact duplicates and missing reworded near duplicate content.
Deduplicating only within one ingestion run instead of across the whole collection.
Waiting until after chunking to deduplicate, multiplying the comparison work unnecessarily.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: Deduplication removes redundant copies before they waste space in the document collection.
The same content often gets ingested more than once from different sources or repeated runs.
Exact duplicates match byte for byte; near duplicates differ only slightly.
Hashing normalized text produces a compact fingerprint for detecting exact matches.
Near duplicates need a similarity measure rather than an exact hash comparison.
Deduplication has to work across sources, not just within a single ingestion run.
Duplicate chunks crowd out diverse, useful results in a retrieval system's top matches.
Deduplicating whole documents before chunking is cheaper than deduplicating every chunk.
